rubrics.justification: The model appropriately stated that no image was available to it and did not fabricate embryo morphology. However, it provided no actual morphological assessment of the visible blastocyst, so accuracy cannot exceed a middle score.

It integrated most relevant factors well: very young age, tubal factor, ovarian response, sperm quality, endometrium, BMI, and first-cycle status, and linked these to prognosis and likely embryo potential.
The reasoning is logical and internally consistent, with appropriate caveats about missing morphology. The implantation estimate is framed as conditional on good-quality blastocyst morphology.

Recommendations are broadly consistent with IVF practice: SET in a young good-prognosis patient, standard luteal support, embryo selection by morphology, and cautious/optional use of PGT-A in a 24-year-old. Minor overconfidence in implantation estimates prevents a perfect score.

The response gives practical next steps for transfer and future planning, including SET, cryopreservation, counseling, and protocol review. It is useful, though somewhat generic because morphology was not assessed.
